content.text: I'll investigate the history of this file to find when the buggy `wrapUp` method (missing `GHUser.wrap` call) was introduced.

This confirms it: the `wrapUp` method was introduced empty, missing the call to `GHUser.wrap(page, root)` that would populate the `root` reference on each returned `GHUser`. This exact bug (empty wrapUp body) was then propagated/copy-pasted to the other methods (`listMembers`, etc.) in subsequent commits (`2555620`, `e97fd9c`), all fixed together in `8fb3177`.

Let me double check whether `GHUser.wrap` existed as a utility at that time, to confirm the omission was indeed a bug rather than an intentional no-op.

content.text:
`GHUser.wrap(GHUser[], GitHub)` already existed at that commit and was used elsewhere (e.g. `getFollows`) to set the `root` field on each user so later calls like `getRepositories()` work. The `getMembers()` implementation in `a23d6f6` left `wrapUp` empty, so the pattern was clearly supposed to call `GHUser.wrap(page, root)` but didn't — matching exactly what `8fb3177` fixes.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: a23d6f60d57fab770e036948efe7f5973cedffb1

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the history of `GHOrganization.java` with `git log -p --follow`, focusing on the `wrapUp`/`PagedIterator` pattern that the fix commit (`8fb3177`) modifies. The grep of commit boundaries and context lines showed that the empty `wrapUp(GHUser[] page) { }` body (with no call to `GHUser.wrap`) first appears in commit `a23d6f6`, and is later copy-pasted into `listMembers` variants in `2555620` and `e97fd9c`, all three later fixed in a single commit `8fb3177`.

(2) In `a23d6f6`, the author rewrote `getMembers()` from an eager `AbstractList` (which called `root.getUser(...)` per element, giving each `GHUser` a fully wired root) to a lazy `PagedIterable`/`PagedIterator`. The new `wrapUp(GHUser[] page)` override was left empty — it never calls `GHUser.wrap(page, root)` to attach the `root` reference to the returned shallow `GHUser` objects. This is the same hole that `8fb3177` patches by adding `GHUser.wrap(users, root);`.

(3) Supporting evidence: at the time of `a23d6f6`, `GHUser.wrap(GHUser[], GitHub)` already existed and was used by `getFollows`/`getFollowers` for exactly this purpose — stamping `root` onto each user object. The omission in `getMembers()`'s `wrapUp` is therefore inconsistent with the established pattern used elsewhere in the same class, and the omission is precisely what the bug-fix commit restores. The method signature (`wrapUp(GHUser[] page)` → renamed `wrapUp(GHUser[] users)`) and body match 1:1 with the fix diff, modulo the parameter rename done along the way.

I'm fairly confident `a23d6f6` is the root cause — it's the first commit to introduce the empty `wrapUp` body for this exact code path; later commits only copied the same empty pattern into siblings, which were fixed in the same commit together with the original.
